trigger: Shopify + ikas + T-Soft normalized-contract pressure showed provider-origin entity timestamps are not guaranteed for every Product/Variant/Inventory/Fulfillment/Shipment observation.

problem.prior_contract: sourceTimestamp was mandatory in TypeScript and NOT NULL in six relational tables.
problem.ambiguity: Canonical specs separated source_timestamp and observed_at but did not define whether observedAt could substitute for absent provider-origin time.
problem.risk: Substituting receipt/capture time for provider-origin time can fabricate freshness and silently misorder out-of-order provider events.

resolution.sourceTimestamp_semantics: Provider/source-origin event/entity/effective timestamp only when explicitly supplied and evidenced by the source/provider.
resolution.substitution_rule: observedAt MUST NOT be copied or relabeled as sourceTimestamp.
resolution.freshness_rule: When sourceTimestamp is unavailable, provider-independent logic must not invent source recency; freshness remains UNKNOWN unless a separate provider-specific evidence rule safely establishes it.
resolution.ordering_rule: Monotonic provider-state advancement requires an incoming sourceTimestamp. Missing provider-origin time does not use observedAt as ordering authority and must fail closed to reconciliation/UNKNOWN.
resolution.relational_change: products, variants, inventory_observations, fulfillments, shipments and operational_events source_timestamp become nullable; observed_at stays NOT NULL.

non_claims: Does not prove provider-authentic E3 mapping.
Does not use observedAt as provider chronology.
Does not mark stale/unknown provider data fresh.
